question: Xi Jinping out before 2027?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if China's General Secretary of the Communist Party, Xi Jinping, is removed from power for any length of time between July 3, 2025, and December 31, 2026, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

CCP General Secretary Xi Jinping will be considered removed from power if he announces his resignation from his role as General Secretary, or is otherwise dismissed, detained, disqualified, or otherwise loses his position or is prevented from fulfilling his duties as General Secretary within this market's timeframe.

The primary resolution source for this market will be a consensus of credible reporting.

eventMetadata.context_description: Xi Jinping’s position as paramount leader remains firmly entrenched ahead of the 21st Party Congress scheduled for late 2027, with recent developments underscoring the absence of credible challenges before year-end 2026. Ongoing anti-corruption purges across the Politburo, Central Committee, and Central Military Commission have removed potential rivals and reinforced loyalty networks, while the new “Xi Jinping Thought on Party Building” doctrine emphasizes centralized discipline. The summer Beidaihe conclave and active leadership signaling focus preparations on extending his fourth term rather than any transition. No designated successor has emerged, and elite dynamics show no organized opposition or institutional pressure for early removal. Although health incidents, abrupt elite realignments, or acute economic shocks could theoretically intervene, current patterns of control and the compressed timeline make such outcomes improbable in trader assessments.
